maml:description.maml:para: Converts YAML text to PowerShell objects, as ConvertFrom-Json does for JSON.

Mappings become PSCustomObjects with properties in file order (ordered hashtables with AsHashtable), sequences become arrays, and scalars resolve through the Core schema to Int64, BigInteger, Double, Boolean, $null or String. Schema Failsafe keeps every scalar a string; Schema Yaml11 reads yes/no/on/off as Booleans. Aliases and merge keys are resolved. Piped lines are joined before parsing, so Get-Content output works directly. Depth sets the deepest nesting accepted (the engine default is 256).
Read every document of a multi-document stream; without it, more than one document is an error.

maml:description.maml:para: Gets nodes of a live YAML document by path, as Path, Value, Node, Line and Column objects.

Select uses the engine's path grammar: dotted keys, [n] for 0-based sequence items, ["key.with.dots"] for keys that are not plain names, and a leading $[n] for the 0-based document in a multi-document stream. Value holds plain PowerShell data as ConvertFrom-OfficeYaml returns it; Node is the live node. Line and Column are 1-based. Without Select, each document's root is returned.

command:example.maml:title: Read the first sheet as objects

dev:remarks.maml:para: Reads the used range of the first worksheet, using the header row as property names.

command:example.maml:title: Find the largest open orders
command:example.dev:code: Import-OfficeExcel -Path .\Reports\Q3-Sales.xlsx -Sheet Orders -Range A5 | Where-Object Status -eq 'Open' | Sort-Object Amount -Descending | Select-Object -First 10 OrderId, Customer, Region, Amount

dev:remarks.maml:para: Reads the Orders sheet from row 5, where the header starts below a title block, and lists the ten largest open orders.

command:example.maml:title: Read a named table
command:example.dev:code: Import-OfficeExcel -Path .\Reports\Helpdesk.xlsx -Table Tickets | Where-Object Status -ne 'Closed' | Group-Object Assignee | Sort-Object Count -Descending | Select-Object Name, Count

dev:remarks.maml:para: Reads the rows of the Tickets table wherever it sits in the workbook and counts open tickets per assignee.

command:example.maml:title: Combine every sheet of many workbooks
command:example.dev:code: Get-ChildItem -Path .\Branches -Filter *.xlsx | Import-OfficeExcel -Sheet * | Export-OfficeExcel -Path .\Reports\All-Branches.xlsx -Sheet 'All branches' -Title 'Branch sales, October 2026'

dev:remarks.maml:para: Reads every worksheet of each branch workbook (each row carries its WorksheetName) and writes one consolidated workbook.

maml:description.maml:para: Combines documents of the same native format in input order.

Supports PDF, Open XML Word and Excel, and YAML files. Binary projection and conversion are not performed. Word, Excel and YAML live documents can receive appended files and remain caller-owned. PDF merging creates a new document, so live PDF targets are not supported. PassThru returns a saved FileInfo for file input or the live document for Document input. PassThruReport returns the native report for PDF file merges and one report per overlay for YAML merges. Native merge options determine which content is imported.

YAML inputs (.yaml and .yml mix freely) are overlaid in order onto the first file or the live document, the way Helm combines values files: mappings merge key by key, sequences follow YamlMergeOptions.Sequences, and only the lines the merge changes differ from the base file.
Refuse to replace an existing destination; requires OutputPath.

maml:description.maml:para: Adds native password encryption or editing restrictions to a document.

Supports PDF and Open XML Word, Excel and PowerPoint packages. Path input is saved in place unless OutputPath names a protected copy. File inputs must be unencrypted: this command has no CurrentPassword parameter. Live Word/Excel restrictions may remain in memory; encryption requires OutputPath or a native associated file path. Encryption is a one-time export, not a stored password setting on the live input. PDF protection returns a new native document with preservation proof, leaving the original live PDF intact. Without Encrypt, PDF restrictions use Password or RestrictionPassword as the owner password and allow opening without a password. With Encrypt, a separate owner password keeps the open password from authorizing permission changes. Unsupported restrictions produce warnings; an entirely unsupported request writes nothing. Safe native signature and preservation policies remain in force.
Caller-owned native document; defaults to the enclosing document content block.
Encrypt the saved artifact using its native engine.

Excel tables accept LegacyPasswordHash, ModifyPasswordHash and ReservedBy; native workbook and reservation property tables are also accepted. PDF tables accept Algorithm, EncryptMetadata, Permissions or AllowedPermissions, and AesCryptographyProvider. Supply PDF passwords through Password and RestrictionPassword. Typed native PDF options retain their owner password, permission mask, algorithm, metadata setting and AES provider.
Protected file destination; accepts exactly one input when supplied.
Emit FileInfo for file input, or the protected native document for Document input.
Open password with Encrypt; otherwise the restriction password. Accepts a credential or warned plain text.
Word editing mode, Excel protection/reservation, or PDF permissions to withhold.
Restriction password, separate from the open password when Encrypt is used; PDF owner password.
